title: Sort Array Using Prefix Reversals
summary: Given an integer array nums that is a permutation of the integers in the range [0, n-1] and an array pre containing valid prefix lengths, determine the minimum number of operations required to sort nums in ascending order by performing prefix reversals.
statement: Given an integer array nums that is a permutation of the integers in the range [0, n-1] and an array pre containing valid prefix lengths, determine the minimum number of operations required to sort nums in ascending order by performing prefix reversals. Each operation involves reversing the first x elements of nums where x is a value from the pre array. If it is impossible to sort nums using these operations, return -1.
constraints: nums is a permutation of 0..n-1 and pre contains allowed prefix lengths.
One operation reverses the first x elements for an x in pre.
Return the minimum operations to sort, or -1 if unreachable.
hints: The state space is finite permutations and every operation has unit cost.
Breadth-first search from the input using each allowed prefix length.
Return the first distance reaching sorted order; return -1 if the queue empties.
BFS explores all states by nondecreasing operation count, so its first target distance is minimal.
editorial: BFS explores all states by nondecreasing operation count, so its first target distance is minimal.

tests.explanation: The permutation is already sorted, requiring zero operations.
